header:
Date: 2026-02-19 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Owen Garcia (Redwood SE); Alex Moreno (Triton Procurement), Dr. Sarah Patel (Triton Security), Michael Cho (Triton CTO), Lina Gomez (Triton Legal)
summary: Procurement intake focusing on pilot pricing, KMS/privileged key handling, egress billing, and routing between hosted/dedicated/private. Triton wants clarity on data residency, SOC2 artifacts, and MSA/DPA exceptions. Agreement to run cost/latency estimate and share DPA excerpt and pilot pricing. Follow-up legal sync requested after internal review.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: okay everyone i think we can get started thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick roll call?
[00:07] Alex: alex here from procurement.
[00:10] Sarah: sarah, security.
[00:12] Michael: michael, cto.
[00:14] Lina: lina legal.
[00:16] Jordan: great, i'm jordan lee, ae at redwood, priya and owen from our se team are on.
[00:22] Priya: hi all, quick note i'll focus on kms, egress and per-token costing for the pilot.
[00:27] Jordan: objective today is to surface procurement blockers — msa/dpa exceptions, kms keying, egress fees and routing (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and to agree next steps for pilot pricing.
[00:36] Michael: high level, we plan to route sensitive workloads through private deployment later, pilot will start on hosted. want to know if that creates double billing for egress or extra kms charges.
[00:48] Owen: good question. for hosted we have an optional customer-managed KMS flow via BYOK — there is a per-key monthly fee and a small keying transaction cost. when you migrate to private the keying is in your VPC, so different billing.
[01:03] Sarah: can you send the concrete numbers? procurement needs the fee schedule. we also need SOC2 type 2 report, pen test summary, and audit log retention durations.
[01:15] Jordan: yes we will attach SOC2 and pentest artifacts. i'll include security-pack.pdf link in the follow-up. audit logs retention is configurable, default 90 days in hosted, enterprise add-on for 365.
[01:28] Alex: procurement will flag anything over $X per month for egress. what is your egress billing model again? we saw something in the deck but it's fuzzy.
[01:36] Priya: egress is charged per GB when data leaves the region or when archived. for hosted it's embedded in the token unit price for small volumes, but beyond threshold we bill separately. for dedicated/private it's per-GB egress plus possible cross-region transfer fees.
[01:50] Michael: we will probably have peak bursts during market open, qps spikes. need to know whether you have routing/fallbacks if hosted capacity is constrained. we can't have requests timing out.
[02:02] Owen: we have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. you can also pin routes to dedicated for SLOs. the canary/fallback policy is configurable per-route in the console.
[02:15] Sarah: on the DPA, we need to see data residency controls and subprocessor list — especially any analytics providers. also can you support customer-managed encryption keys (HSM/KMS) for tokens at rest?
[02:27] Priya: for tokens at rest in hosted we support envelope encryption with customer keys (KMS) and optional HSM integrations for enterprise. subprocessor list will be in the DPA excerpt i'll share.
[02:39] Alex: timeline: procurement wants pricing and legal redlines within two weeks to make a decision. we have a procurement gate on march 5.
[02:47] Jordan: noted. we can aim to get pricing and an excerpt of the DPA + the MSA redline window by feb 21.
[02:54] Michael: question — what about inference quantization and model variants? if you recommend quantized variants, do you guarantee equivalent accuracy for our recommender? we need rollback controls.
[03:06] Priya: we provide quantization profiles and recommend test prompts. rollback and model pinning are supported. quality regressions are monitored via eval hooks. you'll get a recommended profile but the accuracy delta depends on the model architecture and sequences.
[03:22] Jordan: michael, can you share expected sequence lengths and tokens per call? that'll help priya give a concrete cost estimate.
[03:28] Michael: average seq 300 tokens, peak 800 for some flows. estimate 2M tokens/month for pilot, likely scale.
[03:36] Priya: okay i'll run the batching and kv cache config for that distribution and return cost and latency estimates.
[03:42] (brief crosstalk)
[03:45] Lina: legal question — do you accept any non-standard indemnity clauses? our legal team prefers a limited carve-out for algorithmic bias claims.
[03:54] Jordan: our standard msa has limited liability; algorithmic outputs are covered under disclaimers — we can surface the exact clause; non-standard indemnities typically require legal review and exec approval.
[04:06] Lina: also, data subject requests — how quickly can you produce customer logs for audit?
[04:11] Owen: we can produce logs within our SLA window; for hosted standard it's 14 business days, enterprise SLA can shorten that. logs include token-level traces for request ids if requested in advance.
[04:23] Sarah: is token-level logging stored in cleartext? we need to ensure PII is not retained unintentionally.
[04:29] Priya: by default we redact PII and can apply automatic filtering. for enterprise audits you can request raw logs under strict controls and egress via your KMS.
[04:40] Alex: procurement, cost question — if the pilot moves to dedicated mid-pilot, is there a prorated commit or a cancellation fee?
[04:47] Jordan: dedicated requires a reservation window, but for pilots we offer a short-term burst/dedicated lane that is billed at a blended rate; specifics can be in the pilot pricing. there may be a small fee for rapid provisioning but we try to minimize friction.
[05:00] Michael: okay, we need the blended numbers vs hosted to compare.
[05:04] Jordan: will include both in the pricing sheet.
[05:08] Alex: on DPA exceptions — we may need a shorter breach notification window than 72 hours, possibly 48 in our SLAs. is that acceptable?
[05:17] Lina: yes we usually ask for 48 for financials.
[05:20] Jordan: 48 is something we can discuss; standard is 72 but enterprise contracts have been amended to 48 in prior deals, i will flag that with legal.
[05:30] Sarah: any regulatory constraints about data egress from eu to us? we require clear controls — do you support region pinning?
[05:38] Priya: yes region pinning supported; routing policies can pin requests to eu regions only. cross-region fallbacks are configurable but off by default for compliance.
[05:47] Owen: we also have an on-prem package for fully air-gapped deployments if needed for regulated workloads.
[05:53] Michael: if we go air-gapped, what's the onboarding timeline? we're evaluating whether that's feasible within our quarter.
[05:59] Priya: on-prem onboarding usually 8–12 weeks, depends on infra readiness. for pilot we recommend hosted then private long-term.
[06:10] (silence, notes)
[06:15] Jordan: let's walk through the pilot pricing assumptions live so procurement can see line items. i have a shared spreadsheet (pricing-sheet-v3).
[06:23] Alex: yes can you share?
[06:25] Jordan: sharing link in chat... (link pasted) ok open to everyone.
[06:30] Jordan: line one is tokens per month, token unit price, token unit type (generation vs embedding), second tab has egress thresholds.
[06:40] Alex: i see a reserved dedicated column and hosted pilot column, what's the blended rate formula?
[06:44] Owen: blended is time-weighted if you move mid-month: pro-rate reserved commit versus overage on hosted. we'll model a sample transition in the sheet.
[06:54] Lina: legal will need the exact MSA redline window; how long do we get to propose redlines after you submit your standard?
[07:01] Jordan: standard window is 10 business days, we can extend to 15 on request for enterprise.
[07:07] Lina: can we mark a 'no-backend indemnity' clause and ask for narrow carve-outs? we'll send proposed language.
[07:14] Jordan: understood. we'll flag legal for review once you send.
[07:18] Michael: on performance — priya can you give worst-case p95 latency for the quantized model at our seq lengths on a g4-equivalent?
[07:27] Priya: rough estimate p95 for 300 token avg is ~180–220ms on dedicated g4-like instances with batching; hosted may add extra 20–40ms. for 800 token seqs p95 could be 400–600ms unless you increase batch windows.
[07:43] Michael: those numbers are helpful. can you add an estimate for cost per 1k token at those latencies?
[07:48] Priya: yes will include in the cost/latency table.
[07:52] (notes and typing sounds)
[07:56] Alex: procurement — if there's a pilot credit, is that applied to token charges or egress first?
[08:02] Jordan: credits apply to invoice line items per contract; for pilots typically applied to token line until exhausted, then to net balance. we can make it explicit in the pilot term sheet.
[08:12] Sarah: security follow-up: can we schedule a dedicated security deep dive next week? our secops wants to validate key rotation and HSM flow.
[08:20] Jordan: yes we'll put that on the calendar — priya and owen can join.
[08:24] Priya: available next wed and thursday afternoon PST.
[08:29] Alex: wed works for our team.
[08:31] Jordan: noted.
[08:33] Lina: are there any export control clauses we should be aware of?
[08:38] Owen: there are standard export compliance clauses; we'll surface the specific language in the MSA.
[08:43] Michael: one more question — do you have any preferred list of subprocessors that handle analytics or monitoring? procurement asked earlier.
[08:50] Priya: yes list will be in dpa excerpt. typical names are telemetry via our internal pipeline and a small analytics provider for anonymized usage metrics.
[08:58] Jordan: i'm going to summarise next steps now.
[09:02] Jordan: action items — jordan sends pricing-sheet-v3 and dpa excerpt by feb 21; priya runs cost/latency estimate for 2M tokens/month and provides quantization profile; owen prepares KMS transaction fee breakdown. triton legal to send any redline requests; schedule security deep dive next wed.
[09:20] Alex: sounds good, thanks.
[09:22] Michael: thanks everyone.
[09:24] Sarah: thanks.
[09:25] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker mislabels and filler words, some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (k/v vs k v cache, egress tariffs), timestamps approximated.
